text:
Seventeen seconds. That is how long it took Rasmus Dahlin to put Buffalo ahead of the Rangers, and the Sabres never gave the lead back in a 5-1 win. For a team whose week was framed around "team struggles continue," this was a night where the pieces looked like they fit.

The best of those pieces is a line. Jiri Kulich, who started the season slowly, has become a real presence at center between Zach Benson and Tage Thompson, and all three showed up here: Kulich had a goal, an assist and five shots, Benson a goal and an assist, Thompson two assists. Josh Norris scored early in the second for his 200th career point, and Benson tipped in a Dahlin shot 33 seconds later to make it 3-0. Those two goals pushed Buffalo from 70% to 93% to win. Jack Quinn, one of the Sabres' hottest scorers lately, added another in the third, and Kulich beat Joonas Korpisalo from the slot for the fifth.

The score oversells the gap. The Rangers out-attempted Buffalo 58 to 51, shots were even at 30, and by shot quality the Sabres deserved to win about 54% of the time. The difference was in net. Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen stopped 29 of 30, about 1.4 goals better than expected, including an early stop on Glenn Gawdin, the Rangers' surprise two-goal hero against Vancouver. Korpisalo allowed about 2.4 goals more than his 30 shots deserved. New York's lone goal came from Vladislav Gavrikov on a 3% chance late in the second.

For the Rangers, short on bodies with Pavel Dorofeyev on injured reserve and others out for months, it was a flat night that Mike Sullivan will want gone quickly. For Buffalo, a five-goal game from the top of the lineup is the kind of thing that changes how a week feels.
headline: Sabres' new top line buries the Rangers
